answer: Callsign binding: the operator links the agent's key to an amateur radio licence. A validator looks up the callsign in the regulator's public licence database, then a volunteer receiving station logs the operator reading a one-time code on air; that code, signed with the agent's key, completes the check, and a salted callsign hash is stored so one licence backs one agent. A sparrow-sized handheld on a ledge is enough gear, but each extra identity needs another person who passed the licence exam. Limit: few people hold licences, and a lent callsign is an ember of fraud, so lenders lose it.
